importance_rationale: Significant systemic reform addressing a documented structural weakness (researcher mobility in Japan was 0.8 job changes per career vs. 1.6–3.5 in other OECD countries), with potential to improve knowledge transfer and innovation outcomes.
description: The third Science and Technology Basic Plan includes systemic reforms to enhance researcher mobility by expanding fixed-term contracts and performance evaluation at universities and public research institutes, requiring young researchers to change organisational affiliation at least once before obtaining permanent positions, and publishing information on researcher retention rates.
source_quote: Enhance the mobility of researchers by expanding the use of fixed-term contracts and performance evaluation at universities and public research institutes. Require young researchers to change their organisational affiliation at least once after graduation before obtaining a permanent position.

growth_orientation_rationale: University-industry internship programmes and enhanced science education build human capital for innovation and strengthen knowledge transfer between academia and industry, supporting applied research capacity.
package_name: Third Science and Technology Basic Plan
component_name: University human resource development and industry cooperation
status_evidence: Strengthen the role of universities and graduate schools in human resource development, in part through the establishment of long-term internship programmes in co-operation with industry.
importance_rationale: Meaningful reform linking university education to industry needs through internship programmes and competitive funding expansion, addressing documented weaknesses in industry-academia cooperation and science education participation.
description: The third Science and Technology Basic Plan includes measures to strengthen university roles in human resource development through establishment of long-term internship programmes in cooperation with industry, increased support for upper secondary schools prioritising science and mathematics, and expansion of competitive funding for research with improved evaluation.
source_quote: Strengthen the role of universities and graduate schools in human resource development, in part through the establishment of long-term internship programmes in co-operation with industry. Increase support for upper secondary schools that put priority on science and mathematics.

growth_orientation_rationale: Strengthening TLOs and university start-ups facilitates knowledge commercialisation and technology transfer from public research to the private sector, addressing documented weak industry-academia links and low venture capital investment.
package_name: Third Science and Technology Basic Plan
component_name: Technology licensing and university start-up support
status_evidence: Substantially raise the share of private sector-funded research carried out in universities by strengthening ties between industry, university and government through greater support for technology licensing organisations (TLOs), university start-ups and other measures.
importance_rationale: Significant reform targeting a documented structural weakness: business-financed R&D performed by higher education was only 50% of OECD average, and weak industry-academia links limited knowledge transfer and commercialisation.
description: The third Science and Technology Basic Plan includes measures to substantially raise the share of private sector-funded research carried out in universities by strengthening ties between industry, university and government through greater support for technology licensing organisations (TLOs), university start-ups, and other measures.
source_quote: Substantially raise the share of private sector-funded research carried out in universities by strengthening ties between industry, university and government through greater support for technology licensing organisations (TLOs), university start-ups and other measures.

growth_orientation_rationale: Terminating broad tax credits may reduce deadweight losses but could dampen private R&D investment; extending SME support targets smaller firms with financing constraints, supporting innovation but potentially creating distortions.
package_name: R&D Tax Credit and Investment Incentives
component_name: FY2006 R&D Tax Credit Adjustment and SME Extension
status_evidence: The text states 'In the FY2006 budget, the temporary measures were largely terminated as scheduled. However, the R&D investment incentive for SMEs was extended for another two years.'
importance_rationale: An incremental adjustment to an existing tax credit scheme, narrowing the scope to SMEs and introducing new information infrastructure incentives, with smaller projected fiscal impact than the original FY2003 measures.
description: In the FY2006 budget, Japan largely terminated the temporary R&D tax credit measures as scheduled, but extended the R&D investment incentive for SMEs for another two years and introduced new temporary tax incentives for acquiring information infrastructure.
source_quote: In the FY2006 budget, the temporary measures were largely terminated as scheduled. However, the R&D investment incentive for SMEs was extended for another two years, while new measures, including a temporary tax incentive for acquiring information infrastructure, were introduced.

growth_orientation_rationale: Tax incentives for information infrastructure investment reduce the cost of digital technology adoption, supporting private-sector innovation and productivity improvements in the digital economy.
status_evidence: The text states: 'new measures, including a temporary tax incentive for acquiring information infrastructure, were introduced' after FY2006 when the R&D incentive for SMEs was extended.
importance_rationale: A minor, narrowly targeted tax incentive for information infrastructure acquisition. While supporting digital innovation, it is a temporary measure with limited scope compared to broader innovation policy instruments.
description: Japan introduced a temporary tax incentive for acquiring information infrastructure, implemented alongside the extension of the R&D incentive for SMEs after FY2006. This measure aimed to support private-sector investment in digital and information technology infrastructure.
source_quote: new measures, including a temporary tax incentive for acquiring information infrastructure, were introduced.

growth_orientation_rationale: Enhancing labour mobility and career flexibility for researchers increases human capital allocation efficiency and supports innovation capacity in the public research sector.
package_name: 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology
status_evidence: The MEXT launched a project to promote the diversification of the career path for researchers in FY2006 and FY2007.
importance_rationale: A targeted initiative to improve researcher mobility and career flexibility within public research institutes, supporting the broader goal of enhancing innovation capacity. Significant but narrower in scope than system-wide reforms.
description: MEXT launched a project in FY2006 and FY2007 to promote diversification of career paths for researchers at public research institutes, enhancing labour mobility in the research sector.
source_quote: The MEXT launched a project to promote the diversification of the career path for researchers in FY2006 and FY2007.

growth_orientation_rationale: Increasing fixed-term contracts and reducing in-breeding enhances labour mobility, competitive hiring, and performance-based incentives in public research institutions, supporting innovation productivity.
package_name: 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology
status_evidence: Following the 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology (March 2006), research institutes and universities are to increase the number of researchers with fixed-term contracts.
importance_rationale: A significant structural reform of employment practices in public research institutions aimed at improving labour mobility and reducing institutional in-breeding. Affects hiring and career progression across the public research sector.
description: Following the 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology (March 2006), research institutes and universities were directed to increase the number of researchers with fixed-term contracts to enhance labour mobility and reduce in-breeding.
source_quote: Following the 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology (March 2006), research institutes and universities are to increase the number of researchers with fixed-term contracts.

growth_orientation_rationale: Strengthening links between public research and business sectors facilitates knowledge transfer and commercialisation, supporting innovation diffusion and private-sector productivity growth.
package_name: 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology
status_evidence: The 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology promotes co-operation between business and R&D organisations through conferences.
importance_rationale: A targeted initiative to improve university-industry collaboration through structured engagement mechanisms. Significant for knowledge transfer but relatively modest in scope and implementation mechanism.
description: The 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology (March 2006) promoted cooperation between business and R&D organisations through conferences to strengthen links between public research institutes and the business sector.
source_quote: The 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology promotes co-operation between business and R&D organisations through conferences.

growth_orientation_rationale: Combines sectoral R&D investment with human capital development and technology adoption to raise productivity and innovation capacity in service industries, directly supporting GDP per capita growth.
component_name: Toward Innovation and Productivity Improvement in Service Industries
status_evidence: In July 2006, METI announced the programme with detailed action plan and specific targets for 2015.
importance_rationale: A comprehensive sectoral innovation initiative with explicit targets and multi-faceted action plan spanning R&D, human capital, and technology adoption across six service industries, representing significant but focused intervention.
description: In July 2006, METI announced a programme to develop the service industry as part of the 'New Strategy for Economic Growth', selecting six priority areas (health/welfare, childcare, tourism, business services, software contents, distribution/logistics) with a target to increase their market size by 70 trillion yen by 2015. The action plan 'Toward Innovation and Productivity Improvement in Service Industries' focuses on adopting scientific and engineering approaches, utilizing IT, building consumer credibility frameworks, improving quality assurance, developing human resources, facilitating entry, and expanding into foreign markets.
source_quote: In July 2006, METI announced another programme to develop the service industry as part of a comprehensive initiative, entitled the 'New Strategy for Economic Growth'. This programme selected six priority areas for development; health/welfare, childcare, tourism, business services, software contents and distribution/logistics.

growth_orientation_rationale: Strengthens university-industry knowledge transfer and commercialisation of research, which enhances innovation capacity and productivity growth.
package_name: Third Science and Technology Basic Plan FY2006-10
status_evidence: The plan 'aimed at increasing the role of tertiary education in innovation' during FY2006-10, indicating active implementation during this period.
importance_rationale: System-wide reform addressing a structural weakness in Japan's innovation system—the limited role of universities in R&D and weak university-industry knowledge transfer. The plan directly targets institutional mechanisms (IP headquarters, TLOs) to improve commercialisation of research.
description: Japan's Third Science and Technology Basic Plan (FY2006-10) aimed to increase the role of tertiary education in innovation by strengthening ties between industry, universities and government, particularly through greater support for university intellectual property headquarters and technology licensing organisations (TLOs).
source_quote: The third Science and Technology Basic Plan for FY2006-10 aimed at increasing the role of tertiary education in innovation by strengthening ties between industry, universities and the government, in particular through greater support for university intellectual property headquarters and technology licensing organisations (TLOs).

growth_orientation_rationale: Increasing the share of competitive grants improves allocative efficiency in public R&D funding by directing resources to higher-quality research proposals and reducing institutional inertia.
package_name: 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology
status_evidence: The amount of competitive grants rose from 471 billion yen in FY2006 to 477 billion yen in FY2007, boosting its share in central government outlays on science and technology from 12.6% to 13.6%.
importance_rationale: An incremental but meaningful increase in competitive grant funding as a share of total R&D appropriations. Supports the broader policy goal of improving research quality and efficiency through merit-based allocation.
description: The share of competitive grants in central government R&D funding was increased from 12.6% in FY2006 to 13.6% in FY2007, with the amount rising from 471 billion yen to 477 billion yen.
source_quote: The amount of competitive grants rose from 471 billion yen in FY2006 to 477 billion yen in FY2007, boosting its share in central government outlays on science and technology from 12.6% to 13.6%.

growth_orientation_rationale: Improving patent evaluation efficiency reduces transaction costs for innovators and strengthens intellectual property protection, supporting commercialisation of research and innovation incentives.
status_evidence: An action plan to reform the patent evaluation system was updated in January 2007.
importance_rationale: A targeted reform of the patent system to improve evaluation efficiency and reduce barriers to IP commercialisation. Significant for innovation incentives but narrower in scope than broader IP regime changes.
description: An action plan to reform the patent evaluation system was updated in January 2007 to improve the efficiency and framework of patent evaluation.
source_quote: An action plan to reform the patent evaluation system was updated in January 2007.

growth_orientation_rationale: Comprehensive productivity-focused programme combining human capital development, service sector innovation, and university system reform to raise economy-wide productivity and innovation capacity.
status_evidence: The programme was 'presented by the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy (CEFP) in 2007' with explicit goals and action plan components.
importance_rationale: A major, economy-wide productivity enhancement programme with explicit 50% growth target over five years, spanning human capital, service innovation, university reform, and SME competitiveness. Represents structural ambition to reshape innovation and productivity across multiple sectors and institutions.
description: The Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy (CEFP) presented the 'Program for Enhancing Growth Potential' in 2007, aiming to boost productivity growth by 50% for all industries over five years. The action plan includes fostering human capital development, supporting job placement, raising SME competitiveness, pursuing service innovation through IT reform, and expanding the growth frontier by reforming the university system and promoting investment diversification.
source_quote: The 'Program for Enhancing Growth Potential' presented by the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy (CEFP) in 2007. Its goal is to boost productivity growth, as measured by value-added per worker, by 50% for all industries over five years.

growth_orientation_rationale: Provides direct R&D assistance and financial support to SMEs for innovation and productivity improvement, strengthening the innovation capacity of the private sector and supporting firm-level growth.
status_evidence: The project 'was included in Basic Policies 2007' with specified policy tools and objectives.
importance_rationale: A significant SME-focused R&D and innovation support initiative combining financial assistance, R&D support, and human capital development, though narrower in scope than economy-wide programmes.
description: The 'SME Productivity Improvement Project' was included in 'Basic Policies 2007', aiming to enhance productivity of SMEs through IT utilization, corporate revitalization, and promotion of business start-ups. Major policy tools include providing financial support, R&D assistance, and developing human resources.
source_quote: The 'SME Productivity Improvement Project' was included in 'Basic Policies 2007'. This project aims at enhancing productivity of SMEs through IT utilisation, corporate revitalisation and the promotion of business start-ups. Major policy tools include providing financial support and R&D assistance and developing human resources.

growth_orientation_rationale: Sectoral R&D investment in climate and energy technologies builds productive capacity, supports long-term competitiveness, and addresses market failures in green technology development.
component_name: Public R&D investment in climate and renewable energy
status_evidence: Described as launched and implemented in 2008; funding allocation and programme structure explicitly stated.
importance_rationale: Structural, system-wide commitment of $30 billion over five years representing 0.6% of GDP; major sectoral R&D initiative with international technology transfer component.
description: Japan launched the 2008 Cool Earth Promotion Programme, committing approximately $30 billion (0.6% of 2008 GDP) over five years for public R&D investment in climate and energy efficiency technologies to support the transition to a low-carbon society. The programme includes basic and applied research on climate-related technologies, technology transfer to developing countries via a multilateral fund contribution of up to $1.2 billion, and aims to accelerate development of innovative low-carbon technologies to reduce emissions and enhance international competitiveness.
source_quote: In June 2009, Japan established a medium-term target of reducing emissions by 15% from the 2005 level by 2020 (through domestic reductions alone) as a step to its long-term objective of cutting emissions by 60% to 80% by 2050. Price-based measures should be accompanied by other policy instruments... Public investment in R&D, particularly basic research, is important.

growth_orientation_rationale: Counter-cyclical public R&D spending supports both immediate demand and long-term productivity growth through human capital and knowledge creation.
status_evidence: Described as part of fiscal stimulus packages in 2008-09; spending figures explicitly stated.
importance_rationale: Significant increase in R&D spending as part of broader fiscal stimulus, but narrower in scope than a dedicated sectoral programme.
description: Japan increased outlays on education, science and technology as part of its fiscal stimulus packages in 2008-09, accounting for 7.2% of additional spending, intended as a supply-side measure to support both short-term demand and long-term growth potential.
source_quote: Outlays on education, science and technology are significant, accounting for 7.2% of the additional outlays.

growth_orientation_rationale: Reducing regulatory review times and harmonising procedures with international standards lowers barriers to commercialisation of medical innovations, accelerates market entry, and enhances allocative efficiency in the medical device sector.
component_name: PMDA capacity expansion and review process harmonisation
status_evidence: Task force established in 2007; action programme published in 2008; capacity expansion targets for 2010 and 2013 explicitly stated as implemented or in progress.
importance_rationale: Structural reform of regulatory infrastructure for medical devices; significant expansion of PMDA capacity and harmonisation with international standards; multi-year implementation (2007-2013).
description: Japan established a task force in 2007 and published an action programme in 2008 to accelerate medical device reviews and reduce time lags in the commercialisation of new medical devices. The government expanded PMDA (Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency) capacity by increasing reviewers from 35 in 2008 to 104 by 2013, and from 200 in 2007 to more than 400 in 2010 through increased user fees, with recommendations to simplify information requirements, harmonise testing procedures with international standards, and reduce unnecessary re-testing.
source_quote: The key is for global companies to include Japan in their initial development of drugs... One positive step is the decision to increase the number of reviewers in the PMDA from 200 as of 2007 to more than 400 in 2010 by hiking user fees.

growth_orientation_rationale: ETS creates incentives for technology development and knowledge transfer between firms (growth-supporting), but may impose compliance costs and distortions on firms (growth-hindering); net effect depends on design and carbon price level.
component_name: Domestic Crediting Mechanism for SME Technology Transfer
status_evidence: Described as launched in October 2008.
importance_rationale: Significant innovation instrument introducing market-based mechanisms for emissions reduction with technology transfer provisions, but described as a trial system with limited scope.
description: Japan launched a trial emissions trading system (ETS) in October 2008 that includes provisions for domestic crediting mechanisms allowing firms to claim CO2 reductions achieved through joint efforts with SMEs, supported by technology and finance from larger firms.
source_quote: The trial ETS allows participants to use Kyoto mechanism credits and domestic crediting mechanisms, which permit them to claim the CO2 reductions achieved through their joint efforts with small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). Credits are created when SMEs achieve lower emissions...using technology and finance provided by large firms.

growth_orientation_rationale: Attracting high-quality international students to leading graduate schools strengthens human capital for research and innovation, enhancing Japan's research capacity and competitiveness.
status_evidence: The text states 'In 2008, the government launched the Global 30 project' and notes that 13 universities have been selected thus far.
importance_rationale: A significant initiative to internationalise Japan's research and tertiary education system by attracting foreign talent to leading institutions, with dedicated public funding and clear targets, though implementation has been selective.
description: Japan launched the Global 30 project in 2008 to internationalise tertiary education by supporting 30 universities to attract 300,000 foreign students by 2020, with a total budget of 3 billion yen (approximately $37 million).
source_quote: In 2008, the government launched the Global 30 project to help achieve the target of increasing the number of foreign students to 300 thousand by 2020. The project was to support the efforts of 30 universities, with a total budget of 3 billion yen (about $37 million).

growth_orientation_rationale: Facilitates researcher and student mobility and knowledge exchange across borders, strengthening human capital for research and fostering international collaboration in innovation.
status_evidence: The text explicitly states 'A new programme, Campus Asia, was launched in April 2010 with China and Korea'.
importance_rationale: A meaningful regional collaboration initiative promoting academic mobility and knowledge transfer across East Asia through harmonised credit and grading systems, supporting research internationalisation.
description: Japan launched the Campus Asia programme in April 2010 with China and Korea to promote student and academic exchanges by establishing common guidelines on credit transfers and grading policies across tertiary institutions.
source_quote: A new programme, Campus Asia, was launched in April 2010 with China and Korea, and aims at promoting exchanges by establishing common guidelines on credit transfers and grading policies.

growth_orientation_rationale: Increased R&D investment raises productivity and technological capacity, directly supporting the Strategy's target of 2% real annual growth and addressing the baseline 0.8% growth rate through human capital and technology development.
status_evidence: The Strategy was announced in June 2010 with a target to increase R&D spending to over 4% by 2020 through tax and expenditure measures.
importance_rationale: This is a system-wide commitment to increase R&D intensity across the entire economy, representing a structural shift in Japan's innovation investment strategy. The target increase from 3.8% to over 4% of GDP is substantial and aligns with the Strategy's core objective to boost potential growth from 0.8% to 2% annually.
description: Japan's New Growth Strategy targets increased R&D spending from 3.8% of GDP in 2008 to over 4% by 2020 through tax and expenditure measures, with emphasis on science and technology development including ICT to increase efficiency.
source_quote: Total R&D spending is targeted to increase from an already high 3.8% of GDP in 2008 to over 4% by 2020 through tax and expenditure measures.

growth_orientation_rationale: Directed R&D in green technologies creates new markets and employment opportunities while addressing environmental constraints, supporting the Strategy's target of 50 trillion yen in new demand and 1.4 million jobs in green innovation.
status_evidence: In December 2010, the Ministerial Committee on the Global Warming Issue announced a package that includes a 'Green Innovation Strategy' to develop environmental and energy technologies.
importance_rationale: This is a major sectoral R&D initiative targeting a critical area (green technology) with substantial expected economic impact (50 trillion yen demand, 1.4 million jobs). It represents a structural commitment to mission-oriented research aligned with Japan's climate and growth objectives.
description: The New Growth Strategy includes a 'Green Innovation Strategy' announced in December 2010 to develop environmental and energy technologies, supporting the government's objective to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 25% by 2020 relative to 1990.
source_quote: In December 2010, the Ministerial Committee on the Global Warming Issue announced a package that includes the development of a feed-in tariff system, a CO tax and an emissions trading system, and a 'Green Innovation Strategy' to develop environmental and energy technologies.

growth_orientation_rationale: Strengthening R&D budget processes and basic research capabilities enhances innovation capacity and long-term productivity growth.
component_name: Science, Technology and Innovation Strategy Headquarters
status_evidence: The Science, Technology and Innovation Strategy Headquarters was created in 2010 to improve the R&D budget process, strengthen public-private participation and increase basic research capabilities.
importance_rationale: Creation of a new institutional body to coordinate R&D budgeting and strengthen public-private collaboration represents a significant governance reform, though narrower in scope than a comprehensive R&D funding overhaul.
description: Japan created the Science, Technology and Innovation Strategy Headquarters in 2010 to improve the R&D budget process, strengthen public-private participation, and increase basic research capabilities.
source_quote: The Science, Technology and Innovation Strategy Headquarters was created in 2010 to improve the R&D budget process, strengthen public-private participation and increase basic research capabilities.

growth_orientation_rationale: Regional innovation clusters drive competitiveness and productivity by fostering university-industry collaboration and supporting SME innovation in specific fields, contributing to regional economic dynamism.
status_evidence: In 2010, Japan adopted a new approach that promotes regional innovation through clusters, including two national-level programmes.
importance_rationale: Represents a significant shift from top-down national innovation programmes to locally-engaged cluster-based approaches, with meaningful implications for regional competitiveness and university-industry linkages, though narrower in scope than system-wide R&D reforms.
description: Japan adopted a new approach in 2010 promoting regional innovation through clusters, including the New Competitive Cluster Project Start-ups (led by METI) to support SMEs in specific fields, and the Regional Innovation Cluster Programme (directed by the Ministry for Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology) centred around key universities to promote greater university-industry collaboration.
source_quote: In 2010, Japan adopted a new approach that promotes regional innovation through clusters, including two national-level programmes; i) the New Competitive Cluster Project Start-ups, led by METI, to support SMEs in specific fields; and ii) the Regional Innovation Cluster Programme, directed by the Ministry for Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology, centred around key universities to promote greater university-industry collaboration.

growth_orientation_rationale: Attracting foreign R&D centres and high-value-added firms increases domestic innovation capacity, knowledge spillovers, and productivity growth, particularly in services where Japan lags in total factor productivity.
status_evidence: In November 2010, the government announced the 'Inward Investment Promotion Programme' to accelerate FDI.
importance_rationale: Significant policy initiative to attract foreign R&D investment through tax incentives and regulatory reform, with potential for meaningful spillover effects on domestic innovation capacity, though implementation status and scope remain somewhat uncertain.
description: The government announced the Inward Investment Promotion Programme in November 2010 to accelerate foreign direct investment by establishing the world's best investment environment, including corporate tax cuts, economic partnerships, deregulation of investment procedures, and incentives such as preferential tax treatment and subsidies to induce firms to set up Asian headquarters and R&D centres in Japan.
source_quote: In November 2010, the government announced the 'Inward Investment Promotion Programme' to accelerate FDI as well as domestic investment by establishing the 'world's best investment environment'. The programme includes the corporate tax cut, economic partnerships with major countries, deregulation of investment procedures and incentives, such as preferential tax treatment and subsidies.

growth_orientation_rationale: Strengthens the alignment between university education and labour market demands, building human capital for higher value-added activities and facilitating firm-specific skill acquisition.
status_evidence: The text states: 'In 2010, the government launched a new initiative to encourage universities to enhance students' employability by providing more career guidance.'
importance_rationale: A significant initiative addressing the mismatch between tertiary education and labour market demands by strengthening university-industry collaboration on vocational curricula. Supports the New Growth Strategy's goal of creating firm-recognised qualifications, but narrower in scope than system-wide reform.
description: Japan launched a government initiative in 2010 to encourage universities to enhance students' employability by providing more career guidance and involving firms and unions in developing vocational education curricula, with the goal of creating qualifications recognised by firms.
source_quote: In 2010, the government launched a new initiative to encourage universities to enhance students' employability by providing more career guidance. This initiative also involves firms and unions in developing vocational education curricula.

growth_orientation_rationale: Directs credit to growth sectors (health and environment) to stimulate innovation and productive investment, though risks include postponing needed restructuring and resource misallocation through sectoral targeting.
status_evidence: The scheme was introduced in June 2010 and expanded in June 2011 and March 2012, with nearly 3.5 trillion yen disbursed.
importance_rationale: A significant targeted credit facility supporting innovation in designated growth sectors, with substantial funding (5.5 trillion yen by 2012) and multi-year implementation, though narrower in scope than economy-wide R&D policy reform.
description: The Bank of Japan introduced the Growth-Supporting Funding Facility in June 2010, providing long-term low-cost funding to financial institutions to encourage lending to firms in growth industries such as health and environment sectors. The scheme was expanded from 3 trillion yen to 5.5 trillion yen by March 2012.
source_quote: The BoJ introduced the Growth-Supporting Funding Facility in June 2010 to directly encourage banks to lend to firms by providing long-term funding at low costs. The scheme was aimed at firms in growth industries, such as the health and environment sectors.

growth_orientation_rationale: Direct support for university-industry collaboration accelerates knowledge transfer and commercialisation, enhancing firm-level innovation and productivity.
package_name: 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform
status_evidence: The government is supporting university-industry cooperation through a fund of 45 billion yen in FY2012.
importance_rationale: A dedicated fund for university-industry cooperation represents a significant policy instrument for knowledge transfer and applied research, with meaningful economic relevance for innovation ecosystems.
description: Japan established a government fund of 45 billion yen in FY2012 to support cooperation between university research and industry, strengthening knowledge transfer and collaborative innovation.
source_quote: The government is supporting such co-operation through a fund of 45 billion yen in FY2012.

growth_orientation_rationale: Competitive allocation of research funds incentivises research excellence and efficiency, directing resources toward higher-impact research and improving allocative efficiency.
package_name: 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform
status_evidence: The 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform aims at further allocating research funds on a competitive basis.
importance_rationale: A shift toward competitive allocation of research funding represents a significant governance reform affecting the distribution of public R&D resources, with implications for research quality and efficiency.
description: Japan's 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform aims to further allocate research funds on a competitive basis, shifting towards merit-based distribution of public research funding to universities.
source_quote: Boost the share of public research funds for universities that is allocated competitively. The 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform aims at further allocating research funds on a competitive basis.

growth_orientation_rationale: Cooperative graduate programmes build human capital aligned with industry needs and strengthen knowledge transfer, enhancing both research capacity and labour market outcomes.
package_name: 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform
status_evidence: The 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform aims at promoting industry-academia co-operation to respond to labour market demands, in part by implementing graduate school programmes co-operatively with the business sector.
importance_rationale: A structured approach to graduate-level industry-academia cooperation addresses both human capital development and knowledge transfer, with meaningful implications for applied research and firm innovation.
description: Japan's 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform promotes industry-academia cooperation to respond to labour market demands, including implementation of graduate school programmes conducted cooperatively with the business sector.
source_quote: The 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform aims at promoting industry-academia co-operation to respond to labour market demands, in part by implementing graduate school programmes co-operatively with the business sector.

growth_orientation_rationale: Increased public R&D funding to universities enhances research capacity and human capital development, supporting long-term productivity growth and innovation.
package_name: 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform
component_name: Increased public investment in leading universities
status_evidence: Public investment in programmes to create leading universities increased from 12 billion yen in FY2011 to 21 billion yen in FY2012.
importance_rationale: A significant increase in university research funding (75% increase year-on-year) with explicit commitment to competitive allocation, supporting research excellence and institutional capacity-building.
description: Japan increased public investment in programmes to create leading universities, raising funding from 12 billion yen in FY2011 to 21 billion yen in FY2012, with the 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform aiming to further allocate research funds on a competitive basis.
source_quote: Public investment in programmes to create leading universities increased from 12 billion yen in FY2011 to 21 billion yen in FY2012. The 2012 'Action Plan for Higher Education Reform' aims at further allocating research funds on a competitive basis.

growth_orientation_rationale: Provides unlimited long-term funding at low cost to financial institutions to remove financing constraints on credit expansion, potentially supporting innovation and productive investment, though effectiveness depends on whether financing costs are the binding constraint.
status_evidence: The BoJ announced the facility in October 2012 and it began operation in June 2013, providing unlimited long-term funds at 0.1% to financial institutions.
importance_rationale: A significant monetary policy instrument providing unlimited credit at near-zero rates to support lending, with economy-wide scope but narrower innovation focus than direct R&D funding reforms.
description: In October 2012, the Bank of Japan announced plans to establish a new fund-providing measure to stimulate bank lending without setting an upper limit to the total amount of funds supplied, later formalized as the Stimulating Bank Lending Facility in 2012 for implementation beginning June 2013.
source_quote: In 2012, the BoJ announced the introduction of the Stimulating Bank Lending Facility to provide unlimited long-term funds at 0.1% to financial institutions, beginning in June 2013.

growth_orientation_rationale: Direct public investment in industrial competitiveness and innovation is intended to enhance productivity and technological capacity, supporting long-term growth potential.
status_evidence: In January 2013, the new government announced a 10.3 trillion yen fiscal package that includes measures to promote industrial competitiveness and innovation (3.1 trillion yen).
importance_rationale: A significant fiscal allocation to innovation and industrial competitiveness within a broader stimulus package, though the text does not specify the detailed mechanisms or sectoral focus of these measures.
description: Japan announced a fiscal package in January 2013 that includes 3.1 trillion yen (2.2% of GDP) in measures to promote industrial competitiveness and innovation, alongside reconstruction and social spending.
source_quote: In January 2013, the new government announced a 10.3 trillion yen (2.2% of GDP) fiscal package that includes additional funds for the reconstruction of the Tohoku region and disaster prevention (3.8 trillion yen), social spending and regional revitalisation (3.1 trillion yen) and measures to promote industrial competitiveness and innovation (3.1 trillion yen).

growth_orientation_rationale: Energy conservation and alternative energy R&D reduce dependence on imported oil, lowering energy costs and improving allocative efficiency. Applied research in these sectors supports long-term productivity gains and technological capability.
component_name: Alternative Energy Law and Public Corporation
status_evidence: Alternative Energy Law enacted May 1980; Moonlight project operational in FY 1980. Both legislative enactment and immediate implementation in same fiscal year.
importance_rationale: Structural, system-wide reform establishing new institutional framework (public corporation) and major budget increases for energy R&D in response to energy crisis. Combines legislative enactment with substantial funding commitment.
description: Japan enacted comprehensive energy policy legislation in 1980 to address energy constraints through conservation and alternative energy development. The Alternative Energy Law (May 1980) established a new public corporation to lead technological development and commercialisation of alternative energy sources including coal liquefaction, geothermal, and solar energy, with provision of subsidies, debt guarantees, and loans. The 'Moonlight' project, a government R&D programme focused on energy conservation technologies, received substantial budget increases (over 150% to 8 billion Yen in FY 1980).
source_quote: The Alternative Energy Law, enacted in May 1980, calls for the MITI Minister to set and publish overall targets for oil substitution... A new public corporation is being established to play a central role in this area. Its main activities include: technological development related to coal liquefaction, geothermal and solar energy; granting of subsidies and debt guarantees for exploration of geothermal energy sources; and loans and debt guarantees for exploration of overseas coal resources.

growth_orientation_rationale: Directed R&D in new energy sources addresses long-term energy security and technological capability, supporting productivity and innovation.
status_evidence: Text states 'launched' and 'implemented' in 1974.
importance_rationale: Significant sectoral R&D initiative with government and development bank participation, but narrower in scope than economy-wide industrial policy.
description: Japan launched the 'Sunshine project' in 1974 to promote technological research and development for new energy sources, involving participation of the Government and the Japan Development Bank.
source_quote: The 'Sunshine project' aiming at promoting technological research and development for new energy sources was started in 1974 involving the participation of the Government and that of the Japan Development Bank.

growth_orientation_rationale: Directed R&D in energy conservation technology supports productivity improvements and resource efficiency across industrial sectors.
status_evidence: Text states 'launched' in 1978.
importance_rationale: Significant sectoral R&D initiative addressing energy conservation across multiple industries, but narrower than economy-wide policy.
description: Japan launched the 'Moonlight project' in 1978 to promote research and development for energy conservation across industrial sectors.
source_quote: In 1978 a new 'Moonlight project' was launched to promote research and development for energy conservation.

growth_orientation_rationale: Targeted R&D funding and tax incentives for technologically-advanced sectors directly support innovation, productivity, and industrial competitiveness.
status_evidence: Text states 'implemented' in 1974.
importance_rationale: Structural, system-wide industrial policy coordinating multiple funding instruments (grants, loans, tax benefits, joint ventures) across multiple strategic sectors.
description: Japan implemented specific development plans formulated by MITI to promote technologically-advanced industries (industrial machinery, information electronics, aircraft, nuclear energy) through government financial assistance including grants, concessional loans, special tax benefits for R&D projects, and joint ventures to promote domestic technology development.
source_quote: The expansion of technologically-sophisticated industries was promoted by specific development plans formulated by MITI and government financial assistance provided under various schemes. This has essentially taken the form of grants, concessional loans and special tax benefits for research and development projects, as well as joint ventures to promote the development of domestic technology.

growth_orientation_rationale: R&D tax credits and accelerated depreciation reduce the cost of R&D investment and incentivize private sector innovation and technology commercialization.
component_name: R&D Tax Credits and Depreciation Allowances
status_evidence: Text states 'established' without explicit date, but context suggests implementation during 1970s industrial policy period.
importance_rationale: Significant innovation instrument reform providing multiple tax incentives for private R&D, but narrower in scope than comprehensive industrial policy.
description: Japan established R&D tax credits and accelerated depreciation allowances for research and development facilities to support technologically-advanced industries. Lower tax rates were also applied to income received from technology licensed overseas.
source_quote: Government assistance to research and development in these various industries has been channelled through a number of grant programmes and a series of concessional loan programmes from the Japan Development Bank. Significant financial help was also provided through research and development tax credits, the accelerated depreciation of research and development facilities and lower tax rates on income received from technology licensed overseas.

growth_orientation_rationale: Public-private collaboration in software development supports technology transfer, knowledge sharing, and development of advanced computing capabilities.
status_evidence: Text states 'established' in 1979.
importance_rationale: Significant sectoral initiative establishing a new institutional mechanism for public-private collaboration in software development, but narrower than economy-wide reform.
description: Japan established the Information Processing Association (IPA) in 1979 as a joint venture between government and the private sector to promote the development of highly sophisticated computer programmes, supported by the Japan Development Bank.
source_quote: The Government has also directly participated in joint ventures with the private sector such as in 1979 with the setting up of the Information Processing Association (IPA) which aims at promoting the development of highly sophisticated computer programmes.

growth_orientation_rationale: Targeted R&D in advanced semiconductor technology supports innovation in computing and positions Japan competitively in high-technology sectors.
status_evidence: Text states 'implemented' a four-year plan beginning 1979.
importance_rationale: Significant sectoral R&D initiative with multi-year commitment and public-private participation, but narrower than economy-wide industrial policy.
description: Japan implemented a four-year development plan (1979–1983) to develop very large-scale integrated circuitry (VLSI) for extra-high-capacity computers or 'fourth generation' computers, as part of MITI's computer industry development strategy, involving public-private collaboration.
source_quote: Thus, three development plans were elaborated for the computer industry in 1972, 1976 and 1979. The latter covers a four-year project to develop by 1983 very large-scale integrated circuitry (VLSI) to be used in extra-high-capacity computers or 'fourth generation' computers.

growth_orientation_rationale: Directed R&D in nuclear power technology supports energy security, industrial capability, and long-term technological advancement.
status_evidence: Text states 'established' in 1974.
importance_rationale: Significant sectoral R&D initiative with government financial support, but narrower in scope than economy-wide industrial policy.
description: Japan established a development scheme for Light Water Reactor and Nuclear Generation in 1974 to support the nuclear energy machinery industry, providing government financial assistance for R&D in nuclear power plant technology.
source_quote: A development scheme for Light Water Reactor and Nuclear Generation was also established in 1974 for the nuclear energy machinery industry.

growth_orientation_rationale: Co-financed basic research in semiconductors aimed to build technological capability in a strategic, high-value sector, supporting long-term productivity and competitiveness.
status_evidence: Text states the association was established and operated over FY 1976–1979 with government co-financing.
importance_rationale: Structural public-private research programme with significant government co-financing (40%) targeting a strategic technology sector; major initiative for the period.
description: Japan established the Very Large Scale Integrated (VLSI) circuit research association under MITI in 1976, pooling R&D efforts of major semiconductor producers on basic technology with government co-financing of approximately 40% of total R&D costs over the four-year period (FY 1976–1979). This was a major public-private collaborative initiative to advance semiconductor technology.
source_quote: An important factor in the early development of the semi-conductor industry was the Very Large Scale Integrated circuit (VLSI) research association, sponsored by MITI under the Mining and Manufacturing Industry Technological Research Association Law... the total R&D cost over the four-year period the scheme was in operation (FY 1976 to FY 1979 inclusive) was about 75 billion yen, about two-fifths of which was financed by the Government.

growth_orientation_rationale: Direct subsidies for applied R&D in computers aimed to build domestic industrial capability in a strategic, high-technology sector, supporting competitiveness and long-term productivity.
status_evidence: Text states the system was adopted in 1971 and provided subsidies to domestic producers.
importance_rationale: Major sectoral R&D support programme with substantial subsidy rate (50% of development costs) targeting a strategic technology sector.
description: Japan adopted the System of Subsidies for Promoting the Development of Computers in 1971, providing 50% conditional loans for development costs of new computer machines to support domestic producers in competing with Western firms.
source_quote: In 1971, the System of Subsidies for Promoting the Development of Computers was adopted: a 50 per cent conditional loan was provided for the development costs of the new machines.

growth_orientation_rationale: Strategic policy vision identifying knowledge-intensive industries as priorities for development, providing direction for sectoral R&D investment and industrial coordination.
status_evidence: Text states MITI published the Vision in 1970.
importance_rationale: Policy vision document establishing strategic direction; important for framing but not itself a direct funding or implementation mechanism.
description: MITI published a 'Vision' in 1970 highlighting the importance of knowledge-intensive industries, with particular emphasis on coordinating plans for computers and integrated circuits as part of a broader industrial development strategy.
source_quote: The 'Vision' published by MITI in 1970 highlighted the importance of knowledge-intensive industries. In particular, plans for computers and integrated circuits were closely tied together.

growth_orientation_rationale: Subsidies to low-technology, low-profitability sectors may support short-term employment and firm viability but risk allocative inefficiency by directing public R&D resources away from higher-productivity, knowledge-intensive sectors where spillovers and growth potential are greater.
status_evidence: Text uses present tense ('are directed') indicating ongoing practice at time of survey (1985).
importance_rationale: Descriptive observation of subsidy allocation pattern; not a new reform but rather a characterization of existing subsidy distribution.
description: Japan's public R&D subsidies are directed mainly towards low-technology industries such as clothing and footwear, where the small scale and limited profitability of firms constrains investment in developing new technologies.
source_quote: In marked contrast to other OECD countries, public R&D subsidies in Japan go mainly to such low-technology industries as clothing or footwear, where the small scale and limited profitability of firms constrains investment in developing new technologies.

growth_orientation_rationale: Public R&D funding and tax incentives for private research support innovation capacity and human capital development, raising long-term productivity and technological competitiveness.
status_evidence: The text describes these as existing 'major policy instruments for research and development promotion' in Japan, indicating they are in force.
importance_rationale: These are established, multi-instrument R&D support mechanisms spanning both public and private sectors. While not a new structural reform, they represent significant ongoing policy commitment to research and development across basic and applied domains.
description: Japan employs direct research in national organisations, financing of private sector research through the Fiscal Investment and Loan Program, tax privileges for R&D expenditure, and subsidies to basic research such as development of new energy technologies as major policy instruments for research and development promotion.
source_quote: Major policy instruments for research and development promotion are: Direct research in national organisations; Financing private sector research through the Fiscal Investment and Loan Program; Tax privileges for R&D expenditure, and subsidies to basic research such as development of new energy technologies.

growth_orientation_rationale: Tax incentives for technology-enhancing investment directly support productivity growth and capital deepening in response to labour market constraints, raising potential output per worker.
package_name: Labour Shortage Response and Productivity Enhancement (1993)
status_evidence: Text states 'Japan maintained incentives', indicating ongoing implementation.
importance_rationale: Maintenance of existing incentive scheme rather than a new or substantially reformed instrument; incremental policy continuity.
description: Japan maintained tax incentives and support mechanisms for labour-saving and technology-enhancing investment in manufacturing and service industries, recognizing that persistent labour shortages create ongoing motivation for R&D-related equipment investment and productivity-enhancing capital spending.
source_quote: A characteristic of manufacturing investment during the boom was the increasing weight of R&D-related and labour-saving equipment investment. With the labour shortage likely to persist in the long run, the incentive to make labour-saving and technology-enhancing investment continues to be strong.

growth_orientation_rationale: Targeted investment in high-impact technology domains (materials, biotechnology, IT) supports innovation capacity and future competitiveness in strategically important sectors.
component_name: Industrial Science and Technology Frontier Programme
status_evidence: The text describes the programme without explicit evidence of implementation; status inferred as announced pending further evidence.
importance_rationale: A multi-sectoral R&D programme targeting emerging technologies represents a significant but focused initiative rather than a system-wide reform.
description: The 'Industrial Science and Technology Frontier Programme' emphasises research in new materials, biotechnology and information technologies, representing a multi-sectoral R&D initiative addressing emerging technology domains.
source_quote: The 'Industrial Science and Technology Frontier Programme' emphasises new materials, biotechnology and information technologies.

growth_orientation_rationale: Competitive allocation and third-party evaluation improve allocative efficiency and research productivity. Enhanced flows between sectors accelerate knowledge transfer and commercialisation.
package_name: Science Basic Plan and R&D System Reform
component_name: R&D System Integration and Competitive Allocation
status_evidence: Text states 'The government improved' and 'implemented', indicating reforms were in force at time of survey.
importance_rationale: Significant system-wide reform of R&D governance and funding mechanisms, but not a structural creation of new institutions.
description: Japan reformed its R&D system to increase flows of information and researchers among government research laboratories, universities, and businesses. The reform introduced competitive considerations in budgetary allocation and made third-party evaluation of projects obligatory to improve the efficiency of public spending on research and technology.
source_quote: It has also taken initiatives to improve the hitherto compartmentalised R&D system, by increasing the flows of information and researchers among the government research laboratories, universities and businesses, and by enhancing the efficiency of R&D funding through the introduction of competitive considerations in budgetary allocation and the obligation of strict third-party evaluation of publicly funded projects.

growth_orientation_rationale: Increased basic research funding and improved efficiency of public R&D spending enhance long-term productivity and innovation capacity.
package_name: Science Basic Plan and R&D System Reform
status_evidence: Text states 'Japan implemented the Science Basic Plan', indicating the plan was in force.
importance_rationale: Significant policy initiative establishing a strategic framework for basic research, but not a structural institutional change.
description: Japan implemented the Science Basic Plan to promote an open and competitive R&D system, with emphasis on increasing basic research and improving the efficiency of public spending on technology.
source_quote: Science Basic Plan is being implemented to promote open and competitive R&D system (see Chapter IV). This is a promising start.

growth_orientation_rationale: Strengthened IP protection and university commercialisation mechanisms increase incentives for innovation and accelerate technology transfer from research to market, supporting productivity growth.
package_name: University Intellectual Property and Commercialisation Reform
status_evidence: Text states 'The government strengthened' and 'Universities were encouraged', indicating reforms were in force.
importance_rationale: Significant reform of university-industry knowledge transfer mechanisms and IP regime, affecting the commercialisation pathway for public research.
description: Japan strengthened intellectual property protection for innovators and encouraged universities to patent and commercialize their innovative work. The government revised patent-related laws and supported the establishment of Technology Licensing Offices (TLOs) to facilitate the transfer of university research to the market.
source_quote: Universities are now encouraged to have their innovative work patented and sold through a Technology Licensing Office. As well, the patent-related laws have been revised to strengthen the protection of innovators' intellectual property rights.

growth_orientation_rationale: Increased availability of risk capital for innovative ventures supports the creation and scaling of new technology-based firms, enhancing entrepreneurship and innovation-driven growth.
package_name: Venture Capital and Risk Finance Reform
component_name: Venture capital infrastructure and unlisted share market development
status_evidence: Entry [2] states 'implemented'; entry [4] states 'announced'. Taking most advanced status: implemented.
importance_rationale: Significant financial and regulatory reform enabling venture capital supply, affecting the startup ecosystem and commercialisation of innovations.
description: Japan adopted measures to promote the establishment and growth of venture companies by improving the provision of private risk capital. Reforms included easing restrictions on pension fund investment in unlisted shares, creating a special over-the-counter (OTC) market for innovative companies, and implementing measures to facilitate transactions of unlisted shares, supported by financial deregulation.
source_quote: The government has readied the legal and institutional infrastructure for a leap in the supply of risk capital to finance new business ventures, including the easing of the restriction on investment in unlisted shares by pension funds, the creation of a special over-the-counter market for innovative companies, and measures to improve the transactions of unlisted shares.

growth_orientation_rationale: Increased R&D investment and technology development directly raise multi-factor productivity and human capital, reversing decades of factor-intensive growth and enabling sustained productivity gains necessary for Japan's aging economy.
package_name: Structural Reform Programme for Productivity Growth
status_evidence: The survey identifies R&D and technology as essential policy priorities: 'More recent studies have renewed interest in the role of human capital, technology and R&D, and the special role of ICT in stimulating productivity gains.'
importance_rationale: The survey articulates a significant policy priority to reorient growth strategy toward R&D and technology investment as a systemic response to Japan's productivity crisis, though the specific reform instruments and budget allocations are not detailed in this excerpt.
description: Japan's economic survey identifies the need to strengthen R&D and technology as key drivers of productivity growth, emphasizing the role of human capital, technology development, and ICT diffusion in stimulating productivity gains and reversing declining multi-factor productivity trends since 1973.
source_quote: More recent studies have renewed interest in the role of human capital, technology and R&D, and the special role of ICT in stimulating productivity gains. There is in fact a close relationship between the factors touched on above that the Growth Project has served to better substantiate.

growth_orientation_rationale: Performance-based competition for research funding incentivizes universities to improve research quality and productivity, strengthening the knowledge base for innovation.
status_evidence: The government plans to select around ten to twenty Centres of Excellence and allocate more funds to them.
importance_rationale: Significant structural reform introducing competition-based funding to national universities, addressing systemic weaknesses in research incentives and quality. Affects a major portion of Japan's public research system.
description: Japan introduced Centres of Excellence (COE) in national universities, with performance-based fund allocation by third-party assessment to promote competition and improve research quality across ten major subjects.
source_quote: The government plans to select around ten to twenty 'Centres of Excellence' in 10 major subjects based on a performance assessment by a third party, and to allocate more funds to them so as to provide a strong incentive to improve the quality of their research.

growth_orientation_rationale: R&D tax credits and investment incentives are designed to improve firm competitiveness and encourage private-sector innovation, which supports productivity growth.
component_name: R&D tax credits and investment incentives
status_evidence: The ruling parties and the government tax commission want tax credits for R&D and investment incentives for specific goods, with a view to improving the competitiveness of Japanese firms.
importance_rationale: A significant but narrower reform targeting private-sector R&D incentives as part of a broader tax reform package. The planned size of 1 trillion yen (0.2% of GDP) is modest, but the instrument addresses competitiveness concerns.
description: The government proposed tax credits for R&D and investment incentives for specific goods as part of a comprehensive tax reform aimed at improving the competitiveness of Japanese firms.
source_quote: The ruling parties and the government tax commission want tax credits for R&D and investment incentives for specific goods, with a view to improving the competitiveness of Japanese firms.

growth_orientation_rationale: Government support for start-ups (training, loans, subsidies, tax treatment) can stimulate innovation and entrepreneurship; however, the closure of NASDAQ Japan signals market failure in venture capital infrastructure, suggesting structural barriers to scaling innovative firms.
component_name: Government support for start-ups and venture business
status_evidence: Support for start-ups including management training, loans, subsidies and special tax treatment is provided by the government.
importance_rationale: This is a significant but narrowly scoped programme providing multiple instruments (training, loans, subsidies, tax treatment) to support start-ups and venture business. Its impact is limited by structural barriers in the venture capital market, as evidenced by NASDAQ Japan's closure.
description: Japan implemented government support for start-ups and venture businesses, including management training, loans, subsidies, and special tax treatment. However, NASDAQ Japan, one of the three major venture capital stock markets, closed in August 2002.
source_quote: Support for start-ups including management training, loans, subsidies and special tax treatment is provided by the government. NASDAQ Japan, one of the three major venture capital stock markets, closed in August 2002.

growth_orientation_rationale: TLOs reduce transaction costs and information asymmetries in technology transfer from universities to firms, enabling faster commercialisation of research and supporting the creation of innovative startups.
status_evidence: Technology Licensing Offices (TLO) have now been established (there are 27 at present) to promote the transfer of research to firms.
importance_rationale: Establishment of a new institutional mechanism for university technology transfer, modelled on successful US practice. Significant in scope but faces sustainability challenges (public subsidies available for limited period) and ambitious targets may be difficult to achieve.
description: Japan established Technology Licensing Offices (TLOs) to promote the transfer of research results from universities and national research institutes to firms. As of the survey date, 27 TLOs had been established, with government targets set for 1,000 university-derived venture companies within three years and a tenfold increase in intellectual property rights granted by universities within a decade.
source_quote: In recognition of the success of the US system, Technology Licensing Offices (TLO) have now been established (there are 27 at present) to promote the transfer of research to firms.

growth_orientation_rationale: Doubling competitive R&D funding and expanding support for young researchers increases the supply of human capital for research and incentivises research excellence through competition, supporting long-term innovation capacity.
status_evidence: The allocation of public funds to universities via competitive tendering for R&D is to be doubled and the number of young researchers who receive financial support will be increased from the current level of 10000 persons.
importance_rationale: Significant expansion of competitive research funding and young researcher support, addressing human capital constraints in the research system. Doubling competitive funding represents a meaningful shift in allocation mechanisms.
description: Japan increased competitive funding for university research and expanded financial support for young researchers. The allocation of public funds to universities via competitive tendering for R&D is to be doubled, and the number of young researchers receiving financial support will be increased from the current level of 10,000 persons.
source_quote: The allocation of public funds to universities via competitive tendering for R&D is to be doubled and the number of young researchers who receive financial support will be increased from the current level of 10000 persons.

growth_orientation_rationale: The programme aims to foster innovation clusters and entrepreneurship in regions, which could support growth; however, the text expresses concern that the approach may be flawed by attempting to create high-tech parks rather than building on existing local competencies, potentially reducing effectiveness.
status_evidence: In response, METI has launched a programme (Industrial cluster programme) which allows their staff at local offices to play a role of co-ordinator in local clusters.
importance_rationale: A new programme to foster regional innovation clusters through local coordination, addressing the concentration of fast-growing firms in Tokyo and the need for regional dynamism. Significance is tempered by concerns about implementation approach and whether it will build on genuine local strengths.
description: Japan launched the Industrial Cluster Programme through METI, which allows METI staff at local offices to play a coordinating role in developing local innovation clusters. However, the text notes that many projects aim to create industrial parks with a preference for high-tech sectors including biotechnology, rather than building clusters around existing local skills and competencies.
source_quote: In response, METI has launched a programme (Industrial cluster programme) which allows their staff at local offices to play a role of co-ordinator in local clusters.

growth_orientation_rationale: Removing barriers to university-industry collaboration enhances knowledge transfer and commercialization of research, supporting innovation-driven productivity growth.
status_evidence: The text states 'The government's move to create a more open and transparent industry-science relationship and to remove the disincentives to co-operation facing the universities and the NRIs goes in the right direction.'
importance_rationale: A significant institutional reform addressing structural barriers to university-industry collaboration, though the text notes it is 'too early to judge the effectiveness of the measures taken.' The reform targets a key bottleneck in Japan's innovation system.
description: The government moved to create a more open and transparent industry-science relationship and to remove disincentives to cooperation facing universities and national research institutions (NRIs), aiming to strengthen university-industry collaboration in R&D.
source_quote: The government's move to create a more open and transparent industry-science relationship and to remove the disincentives to co-operation facing the universities and the NRIs goes in the right direction.

growth_orientation_rationale: TLOs facilitate technology transfer and spinoff creation, converting academic research into commercial innovation and supporting entrepreneurship-driven growth.
status_evidence: The text references 'university TLOs' as an existing policy tool being deployed to promote regional dynamism and new start-ups.
importance_rationale: A significant institutional innovation supporting knowledge commercialization and startup creation. However, the text cautions against setting administrative targets for university-based startups, suggesting implementation challenges.
description: The government is establishing university technology licensing offices (TLOs) to facilitate commercialization of university research and support new startup creation from academic institutions.
source_quote: university TLOs are also viewed in this manner. More attention needs to be paid to facilitating or invigorating existing national clusters based on current skills

growth_orientation_rationale: Strengthening university research capacity and postgraduate education builds human capital for innovation and enhances the supply of skilled researchers, supporting long-term productivity growth.
status_evidence: The text states 'Reform of the universities is important but in an attempt to establish premium institutions for research and teaching, care will have to be taken that assessment is at arms length.'
importance_rationale: A significant structural reform of the university system aimed at improving research quality and human capital development. The text emphasizes the need for arm's-length assessment to ensure substantive rather than merely formal reform.
description: The government is reforming universities to establish premium institutions for research and teaching, with emphasis on improving research quality and expanding postgraduate education.
source_quote: Reform of the universities is important but in an attempt to establish premium institutions for research and teaching, care will have to be taken that assessment is at arms length. Above all they should focus on quality research and expand post-graduate education.

growth_orientation_rationale: Shifting from block funding to competitive allocation improves allocative efficiency and incentivizes higher-quality research outcomes.
package_name: Third Science and Technology Basic Plan (FY2006-10)
status_evidence: The text presents this as a recommendation within the assessment of the third Basic Plan, indicating it is a policy direction being advocated.
importance_rationale: A significant but narrower reform targeting the allocation mechanism of existing R&D budgets. Increasing competitive grants from 13% to a higher share would meaningfully improve research efficiency without expanding total funding.
description: The OECD recommends that Japan increase the share of competitive grants in public R&D fund allocation to enhance spending efficiency, noting that competitive grants accounted for only 13% of total R&D funding in FY2005.
source_quote: Increase further the share of competitive grants in the allocation of public R&D funds to enhance the efficiency of spending. In FY2005, competitive grants accounted for only 13% of the total.

growth_orientation_rationale: Increased researcher mobility between sectors facilitates knowledge transfer, reduces institutional rigidities, and enables better matching of talent to research opportunities, enhancing innovation productivity.
status_evidence: The text presents this as a priority recommendation for upgrading innovation-specific policies, not yet implemented.
importance_rationale: A significant structural reform addressing a key constraint on innovation (low researcher mobility, with fewer than one job change per career on average). Addresses both human capital and knowledge transfer dimensions.
description: The OECD recommends that Japan strengthen links between government, academic, and business research sectors by increasing researcher mobility through pension portability reform, performance-based pay, fixed-term contracts, and improved job opportunity information.
source_quote: One priority should be to strengthen links between research institutes in government, academia and business sectors. This requires greater mobility of researchers, given that the average number of job changes by researchers during their career is less than one in Japan.

growth_orientation_rationale: Redirecting R&D support toward start-ups rather than incumbents encourages entrepreneurship, creative destruction, and the commercialization of new technologies, supporting dynamic productivity growth.
status_evidence: Presented as a recommendation for improvement in the assessment of the third Basic Plan.
importance_rationale: A significant reorientation of R&D support allocation toward start-ups, addressing a structural bias toward incumbent firms. This would shift innovation incentives toward new entrants and commercialization.
description: The OECD recommends that Japan focus R&D support on new start-ups rather than existing companies, as part of broader innovation policy improvements outlined in the assessment of the third Science and Technology Basic Plan.
source_quote: Focus support for R&D on new start-ups rather than on existing companies as is now the case.

growth_orientation_rationale: Broadening the policy council's mandate to address framework conditions (regulation, competition, institutional coordination) removes barriers to innovation diffusion and commercialization.
component_name: Council for Science and Technology Policy mandate expansion
status_evidence: Presented as a recommendation for improvement in the assessment of the third Basic Plan.
importance_rationale: A minor institutional reform expanding the scope of an existing governance body. While potentially beneficial for policy coordination, it is narrower in scope and impact than direct R&D funding or instrument reforms.
description: The OECD recommends that Japan expand the work of the Council for Science and Technology Policy beyond purely scientific issues to include measures improving framework conditions for innovation, such as regulatory reform and institutional coordination.
source_quote: Expand the work of the Council for Science and Technology Policy beyond purely scientific issues to include measures to improve framework conditions for innovation.

growth_orientation_rationale: Strengthening international research links and IP flows facilitates knowledge spillovers, technology transfer, and access to global research networks, enhancing innovation capacity.
status_evidence: Presented as a recommendation for improvement in the assessment of the third Basic Plan.
importance_rationale: A minor policy recommendation addressing international research collaboration. While relevant to innovation, it is narrower in scope and does not represent a major structural reform.
description: The OECD recommends that Japan strengthen international research links and increase foreign ownership of domestic inventions and domestic ownership of foreign inventions, noting that both are the lowest in the OECD area according to patent data.
source_quote: Strengthen international links. According to data on patents, foreign ownership of domestic inventions in Japan and domestic ownership of foreign inventions are both the lowest in the OECD area.

growth_orientation_rationale: Expanding competitive funding mechanisms with improved evaluation improves allocative efficiency in public R&D spending, directing resources toward higher-quality research and reducing wasteful spending.
package_name: Third Science and Technology Basic Plan
