status_evidence: Presented as a recommendation within the third Science and Technology Basic Plan.
importance_rationale: A significant reform of the public R&D funding system, addressing resource allocation efficiency through competitive mechanisms and improved evaluation. Affects the broader research funding landscape.
description: The third Science and Technology Basic Plan emphasises further expansion of competitive funding for research based on improved evaluation of such programmes, aiming to allocate R&D resources more efficiently across priority areas.
source_quote: Further expand the use of competitive funding for research, based on improved evaluation of such programmes.

growth_orientation_rationale: Facilitating longer stays and easier permanent residence for foreign researchers enhances Japan's ability to attract international talent, strengthening research capacity and knowledge networks.
package_name: Third Science and Technology Basic Plan
status_evidence: Presented as a policy recommendation within the third Science and Technology Basic Plan.
importance_rationale: A targeted reform addressing researcher mobility and international collaboration, key weaknesses in Japan's innovation system. Affects human capital and international research linkages.
description: The third Science and Technology Basic Plan proposes to strengthen international linkages by extending the length of time that foreign researchers may stay in Japan and relaxing requirements for obtaining permanent residence permits, aimed at enhancing researcher mobility and international collaboration.
source_quote: Extend the length of time that foreign researchers may stay in Japan and relax the requirements for obtaining permanent residence permits.

growth_orientation_rationale: Reducing patent examination delays lowers transaction costs for innovators and accelerates the commercialization of inventions, supporting innovation-driven growth.
status_evidence: METI has set an objective of reducing waiting time to 11 months by 2013, primarily by hiring more staff.
importance_rationale: A significant but targeted reform addressing a specific bottleneck in the innovation system. Reducing patent examination delays is important for commercialization efficiency but narrower in scope than system-wide changes.
description: Japan set an objective to reduce patent examination waiting time from 27 months to 11 months by 2013, primarily through hiring additional staff at the patent office.
source_quote: METI has set an objective of reducing the exceptionally long waiting time for patent examination, which has recently increased to 27 months, to 11 months by 2013, primarily by hiring more staff.

growth_orientation_rationale: Filtering low-quality patents may improve patent system efficiency and reduce frivolous filings, but may increase filing costs and deter some legitimate innovation disclosure, creating trade-offs.
status_evidence: In addition, it is considering discouraging companies from requesting examination of patents which may lack novelty and inventive step.
importance_rationale: A minor, targeted policy adjustment aimed at improving patent examination efficiency. While relevant to innovation governance, it is narrower in scope and impact than major system reforms.
description: Japan is considering discouraging companies from requesting examination of patents lacking novelty and inventive step, as part of efforts to improve the patent system and reduce examination backlogs.
source_quote: In addition, it is considering discouraging companies from requesting examination of patents which may lack novelty and inventive step.

growth_orientation_rationale: Science and technology investment enhances productivity and international competitiveness, supporting long-term GDP growth and Japan's position in global markets.
component_name: Third Basic Plan for Science and Technology
status_evidence: The Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy published the Globalisation Strategy in May 2006, which includes implementation of the third Basic Plan for science and technology.
importance_rationale: The inclusion of science and technology in Japan's flagship Globalisation Strategy signals commitment to R&D as a competitiveness driver, though the specific details and budget allocation are not provided in this text.
description: Japan's Globalisation Strategy (May 2006) includes a commitment to implement the third Basic Plan for science and technology as part of efforts to strengthen international competitiveness. This positions science and technology development as a key pillar of Japan's global economic integration strategy.
source_quote: Implement the third Basic Plan for science and technology (see Chapter 5).

growth_orientation_rationale: Attracting top research talent and improving human capital supply enhances innovation capacity and productivity growth, supporting Japan's competitiveness in knowledge-intensive sectors.
status_evidence: The Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy published the Globalisation Strategy in May 2006, which includes proposals to establish an environment attracting outstanding talent including researchers and students.
importance_rationale: Immigration and talent attraction reforms are significant for building research capacity and international competitiveness, though implementation details and budget commitments are not specified in this excerpt.
description: Japan's Globalisation Strategy (May 2006) proposes to establish an environment that attracts outstanding talent from other countries, including researchers and students, and to improve the immigration system to increase the inflow of highly qualified human resources for research and innovation.
source_quote: Establish an environment that attracts outstanding talent from other countries, including researchers and students. Improve the immigration system in order to increase the inflow of highly qualified human resources.

growth_orientation_rationale: R&D tax subsidies reduce the cost of innovation for firms, incentivizing private investment in research and development, which raises productivity and long-run output per capita.
status_evidence: The text references the tax subsidy and its estimated effects but does not explicitly state the implementation, legislation, or announcement date.
importance_rationale: The R&D tax subsidy is a significant innovation instrument with measurable effects on private R&D spending (8% increase per 10% subsidy increase), but the text provides limited detail on scope, duration, or systemic impact.
description: Japan implemented a tax subsidy for R&D designed to incentivize private-sector research and development spending. A permanent 10% increase in the tax subsidy was estimated to raise R&D spending by over 8%.
source_quote: A permanent 10% increase in the tax subsidy for R&D was estimated to raise the level of R&D spending by over 8% (Jaumotte and Pain, 2005).

growth_orientation_rationale: Improving disclosure encourages private investment in venture businesses and reduces reliance on public guarantees, supporting market-driven allocation of capital to innovative startups.
component_name: Firm disclosure improvement for venture investment
status_evidence: Disclosure by firms has been improved to encourage investment by individual investors in venture businesses.
importance_rationale: A targeted reform to improve venture capital market functioning through enhanced transparency. Supports the transition from public debt guarantees to market-based venture financing.
description: Disclosure by firms was improved to encourage investment by individual investors in venture businesses, supporting the development of venture capital markets while moving away from public debt guarantees.
source_quote: Disclosure by firms has been improved to encourage investment by individual investors in venture businesses.

growth_orientation_rationale: Public investment in basic energy R&D addresses market failures in fundamental research and supports long-term technological innovation.
component_name: Direct public investment in energy R&D
status_evidence: Phrased as a recommendation ('should invest'); no evidence of government adoption or implementation.
importance_rationale: Recommendation or proposal not yet adopted; no specific budget or implementation timeline provided.
description: Japan should invest directly in basic R&D for energy-related technologies to share the risk of developing new technologies with the private sector and achieve innovations necessary to meet targeted emission reductions.
source_quote: Specific policies, in addition to price-based instruments, are needed therefore to foster R&D and the development of renewable energy sources. In particular, the government should invest directly in basic R&D to share the risk of developing new technologies with the private sector.

growth_orientation_rationale: Strengthening higher education's contribution to innovation supports productivity growth and human capital development, essential to offset declining working-age population and achieve 2% growth target.
status_evidence: The New Growth Strategy aims to increase the role of higher education in innovation; text indicates this is part of government strategy but does not confirm implementation.
importance_rationale: Significant policy objective within the broader New Growth Strategy to link higher education to innovation and growth, but the text provides limited detail on specific mechanisms or funding commitments.
description: Japan's New Growth Strategy aims to increase the role of higher education in innovation as part of broader efforts to accelerate economic growth to 2% in the 2010s through green innovation, expanded health care, and regional development.
source_quote: The New Growth Strategy also aims to increase the role of higher education in innovation. Education in Japan is outstanding both in terms of quantity and quality.

growth_orientation_rationale: Increasing public R&D investment expands the knowledge base and innovation capacity, supporting long-term productivity growth.
status_evidence: Listed as supply-side policy objective 17 in the New Growth Strategy framework.
importance_rationale: A major structural commitment to increase national R&D spending intensity to 4% of GDP represents a significant system-wide policy change with broad implications for research capacity and innovation ecosystem.
description: Japan plans to increase R&D investment to at least 4% of GDP as part of its supply-side policy agenda.
source_quote: 17. Increase R&D investment to at least 4% of GDP

growth_orientation_rationale: Enhanced researcher mobility and competitive funding mechanisms improve knowledge flows between academia and industry, and allocate research resources more efficiently toward innovation.
component_name: University R&D strengthening and researcher mobility
status_evidence: Discussed as part of the New Growth Strategy's objective to increase universities' role in innovation through structural reforms.

source_quote: Enhance the role of the tertiary sector in innovation, in part through greater co-operation between universities and the business sector, including enhanced labour mobility of researchers.

growth_orientation_rationale: Increased public R&D funding and reallocation from defence to civilian research enhances productivity, innovation capacity, and commercial applications, supporting long-term GDP growth.
status_evidence: Description [5] explicitly states 'plans to increase' (future commitment); descriptions [0] and [3] describe ongoing or committed policies.
importance_rationale: Structural reorientation of federal R&D spending priorities and commitment to increased civilian research funding represents a system-wide policy shift with significant macroeconomic implications.
description: The U.S. federal government committed to increased public expenditure for basic and civilian research and development as part of structural reform initiatives. The federal government sponsors approximately half of total national R&D investment (1.5% of GNP), with plans to increase support for civilian R&D faster than defence-oriented R&D going forward to improve overall R&D productivity and commercial orientation.
source_quote: The federal government has been actively involved in sponsoring this type of research, to the extent that half of total national investment in R&D (amounting to about 1½ per cent of GNP) is paid for by the federal government.

growth_orientation_rationale: Increased public investment in basic research enhances the knowledge base and technological capabilities that underpin long-term productivity growth and innovation.
status_evidence: The text states that steps taken by the United States include 'an increase in government expenditure for basic research and development' as part of measures to address competitiveness.
importance_rationale: A significant but narrower initiative to boost basic research funding as part of a broader competitiveness strategy. The reform addresses a key input to innovation but is presented as one component among several policy measures.
description: The United States increased government expenditure for basic research and development as part of a broader competitiveness strategy, alongside an extension of the R&D tax credit for another year.
source_quote: Steps taken by the United States include: federal deficit control, as embodied in the Budget Act; an increase in government expenditure for basic research and development; an extension of the R&D tax credit for another year.

growth_orientation_rationale: Redirecting R&D from defence to civilian applications increases spillovers to commercial sectors and improves productivity growth. CRADAs strengthen knowledge transfer between public research institutions and private firms.
component_name: Reorientation of federal R&D from defence to civilian and dual-use technologies
status_evidence: The text states 'Henceforth, federally-funded mission-oriented R&D will be used to try to improve the productivity of private R&D. Accordingly, the share of purely military R&D is being cut back, and resources are being directed to civilian and dual-use technologies.'
importance_rationale: This represents a structural reorientation of U.S. federal R&D policy, shifting the allocation of nearly $70 billion in annual federal R&D spending away from defence (which represented 29% of total R&D) toward civilian applications. The reform affects multiple federal agencies and establishes a new governance framework (CRADAs) for public-private collaboration, with over 1,500 agreements valued at $323 million already in place by 1992.
description: The new Administration redirected federal R&D spending away from defence-related research toward civilian and dual-use technologies by reforming national laboratories and the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, and mandating increased R&D cooperation with industry through CRADAs (cooperative research and development agreements).
source_quote: Henceforth, federally-funded mission-oriented R&D will be used to try to improve the productivity of private R&D. Accordingly, the share of purely military R&D is being cut back, and resources are being directed to civilian and dual-use technologies by reforming existing agencies (national laboratories and the former Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency).

growth_orientation_rationale: Investment in high-performance computing infrastructure and information networks enhances research capacity and enables knowledge creation and diffusion, supporting long-term productivity growth.
component_name: High Performance Computing and Information Infrastructure
status_evidence: The text states the government 'will provide funding' for pilot projects and computing infrastructure, indicating announced policy.
importance_rationale: A significant infrastructure investment supporting research and innovation through high-performance computing and information networks, with applications across education and health sectors.
description: The government will provide funding for pilot projects in education and health-care spheres and $784 million over four years for 'cross-cutting high performance computing' as part of establishing a national information infrastructure.
source_quote: $784 million over the next four years for related 'cross-cutting high performance computing'

growth_orientation_rationale: Redirects substantial public R&D resources from defence to civilian applications, potentially improving allocative efficiency and private-sector innovation capacity through knowledge transfer and collaborative research.
component_name: National laboratories partnerships and dual-use R&D matching grants
status_evidence: The text states 'For fiscal 1993 it includes $1.4 billion appropriated by Congress last year, but not spent, plus another $0.3 billion,' indicating the programme was in effect during the 1993 fiscal year.
importance_rationale: This is a major structural reform redirecting a significant portion of federal R&D spending ($20 billion over five years) from defence to civilian applications. It represents a system-wide reorientation of national R&D priorities and involves substantial institutional partnerships across 726 national laboratories and private industry, with lasting implications for the innovation ecosystem.
description: The Administration proposed the Defence Reinvestment and Conversion Initiative, a $20 billion package over five years (rising to $5.2 billion in FY 1997) designed to redirect federal R&D away from defence towards civilian applications. The initiative includes 29 programmes, with a focus on partnerships between industry and 726 national laboratories for dual-use technology development and matching grants for industry-led R&D.
source_quote: The Administration has proposed the Defence Reinvestment and Conversion Initiative to ease the transition. It embodies 29 different programmes... there are a series which will try to set up partnerships between industry and the 726 national laboratories (that do some $23 billion or about 13 per cent of the nation's total R&D), especially for dual-use technology, and provide matching grants for industry-led R&D.

growth_orientation_rationale: Investment in math-science research and education builds human capital and scientific capacity, which are foundational to long-term productivity growth and innovation.

description: The federal government proposed expansion of math-science education research funding, allocating $100-200 million in 1994 as part of a broader human capital and education initiative.
source_quote: math-science education research ($100-200 million in 1994)

growth_orientation_rationale: Public funding for pre-competitive generic R&D addresses market failures where social returns exceed private returns, stimulating private R&D efforts and generating significant spillovers to the broader economy.

importance_rationale: A significant expansion of an existing programme (NIST's Advanced Technology Program) with substantial budgetary increase (nearly 100% increase), targeting pre-competitive generic technologies where market failures justify public intervention. The reform reflects a shift toward greater government activism in technology policy.
description: The new Administration proposed a major budgetary increase of $535 million in FY 1994 (nearly double the prior year's allocation) for the National Institute of Standards and Technology to expand its Advanced Technology Program, which develops high-risk generic pre-commercial and pre-competitive technologies with partial private-sector funding.
source_quote: The new Administration has also indicated a willingness to move toward greater activism by proposing a major budgetary increase ($535 million in FY 1994, nearly double this year's allocation) for the National Institute of Standards and Technology to proceed with its Advanced Technology Program to develop high-risk generic technologies.

source_quote: Substantial amounts are to be made available for transportation infrastructure... environmental protection, rural development, energy research and conservation...

New rules confine its availability to domestic research, intended to induce marginal increases in equipment investment to incorporate R&D output.
source_quote: The temporary extension of the Research and Experimentation Tax credit (see below) and new rules confining its availability to domestic research may induce a marginal increase in equipment investment to incorporate the R&D output, a few years hence.

growth_orientation_rationale: Both initiatives target strategic sectors (aerospace, semiconductors/displays) where domestic capability and competitiveness are critical for long-term productivity and technological leadership.
status_evidence: Index 4 explicitly states 'announced a plan'; index 2 states 'awarded', suggesting implementation has begun, but both are announced in 1994.

source_quote: The Defense Department announces a plan to spend $587 million over the next five years (and eventually a total of $1 billion) to support the development of a domestic industry to produce flat-panel display screens.

description: The Administration proposed to make the Research and Experimentation tax credit (established in 1981) permanent, which would enhance its effectiveness in incentivizing private R&D spending. The credit had been extended and modified multiple times, with its temporary nature criticized for biasing firms away from long-term projects.
source_quote: The Administration proposed to make the credit permanent which would have served to enhance its effectiveness, but Congress extended it only through June 1995. Others have suggested that it should be made available to commercialisation expenditures as well.

growth_orientation_rationale: Increased public R&D funding expands the knowledge base and research capacity, supporting long-term productivity growth and innovation.

source_quote: The emphasis of fiscal policy has been on higher expenditures. The increase in budget outlays covers a wide range including defence, space programmes, education and research, foreign aid, housing and community development.

description: The August 1981 Economic Recovery Tax Act introduced a 25 percent tax credit for incremental research and development costs, reducing the effective cost of R&D investment for firms.
source_quote: A 25 percent credit for incremental research and development costs.

growth_orientation_rationale: Technology transfer programmes and sectoral focus on semiconductors and superconductivity support commercialisation of R&D, raising productivity and competitive advantage in high-value sectors.
package_name: Omnibus Trade and Competitiveness Act of 1988
component_name: Commercialising R&D — technology transfer centres and sectoral commissions
status_evidence: Text states 'established' and 'created' in past tense, and explicitly notes 'legislated' status; Act passed in 1988.

The Act created a National Advisory Committee on Semiconductors and mandated a national commission on Superconductivity to ensure U.S. leadership in semiconductor and superconducting technology development and application.
source_quote: A significant proportion of the Trade Act (the Omnibus Trade and Competitiveness Act) addresses the issue of improving the commercialisation of U.S. R&D effort. New programmes are directed at the rapid transfer of technology to industry, via regional centres intended to provide direct support to small and medium-sized manufacturing firms.

status_evidence: Text presents this as a policy position or recommendation ('needs to be corrected') without evidence of legislative action or implementation.

source_quote: There remain a number of general structural impediments to better productivity performance, such as low savings and the associated high cost of capital, and insufficient investment in general education, skill development and commercial R&D, which need to be corrected.

growth_orientation_rationale: Targeted sectoral R&D in semiconductors and superconductivity addresses strategic technology gaps and supports competitive advantage in high-value industries, enhancing long-term productivity.
status_evidence: The 1988 Trade Act created these institutions; status is implemented as of the 1990 survey date.
importance_rationale: Creation of major sectoral R&D institutions (Sematech, superconductivity commission) through legislation represents a structural policy intervention in critical technology domains.
description: The 1988 Trade Act created the National Advisory Committee on Semiconductors (Sematech) to ensure U.S. supremacy in semiconductor technology and mandated creation of a national commission on superconductivity to promote U.S. leadership in that area.
source_quote: The 1988 Trade Act took a step towards intervention by creating a National Advisory Committee on Semiconductors (Sematech), with the aim of ensuring U.S. supremacy in semiconductor technology. It also mandated the creation of a national commission on superconductivity in order to promote U.S. leadership in this area.

description: Congress expanded the Defence Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) mandate to provide venture capital funding for government-industry consortia developing advanced technologies including semiconductors, high-definition television (HDTV), superconductivity, and artificial intelligence.
source_quote: Subsequently funds have been channelled into high-definition television (HDTV), superconductivity and artificial intelligence through the Defence Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA), which finances the government-industry consortium for developing semiconductor manufacturing technology. Congress expanded DARPA's mandate to allow it to provide venture capital.

source_quote: Defence R&D activities have been managed so as to exploit commercial applications. Significant advances in civil aviation and medical technology have had their origin in defence-sponsored R&D, as have civilian use of lasers, integrated circuits and weather satellites.

source_quote: The Administration intends to promote 'Regional Technology Alliances' and 'Agile Manufacturing Programs' in order to assist in the exploitation of network externalities, and technology outreach or extension centres to stimulate technology transfer and ensure diffusion of innovations.

description: The Administration proposed setting up technology outreach or extension centres to alleviate problems of exploiting and diffusing existing technology.
source_quote: The problems of exploiting and diffusing existing technology could be alleviated by the proposed setting-up of technology outreach or extension centres.

growth_orientation_rationale: Redirecting R&D from defence to civilian and dual-use technologies increases commercial spillovers and productivity growth; closer lab-industry cooperation accelerates technology transfer and commercialisation.
component_name: National Laboratories-Industry Cooperation and Civilian R&D Shift
status_evidence: Text states 'direct federal outlays are set to shift to civilian and dual-use technologies. Also worthwhile is the closer co-operation between the national laboratories and private industry' — framed as Administration policy direction.
importance_rationale: A significant reorientation of national laboratory R&D toward civilian applications and private-sector collaboration. Reflects a structural shift in R&D priorities but implementation depends on budget allocation decisions.
description: The Administration proposed closer cooperation between national laboratories and private industry to shift federal R&D spending from defence-related projects toward civilian and dual-use technologies.
source_quote: To this point too much of the nation's R&D spending has been devoted to defence-related projects, and direct federal outlays are set to shift to civilian and dual-use technologies. Also worthwhile is the closer co-operation between the national laboratories and private industry.

growth_orientation_rationale: Reduces legal barriers to private R&D collaboration, enabling firms to pool resources and share knowledge in pre-competitive research, which increases innovation efficiency and reduces duplication.
status_evidence: Over 300 R&D joint ventures have been registered under the Act, with concentration in information technology, biotechnology and new materials.
importance_rationale: Structural reform eliminating antitrust barriers to private R&D collaboration. Enabled a new governance model for pre-competitive research across multiple sectors, with sustained uptake (300+ ventures registered by 1993). Addresses a fundamental market failure in knowledge creation.
description: The 1984 National Co-operative Research Act eliminated private antitrust risks for R&D joint ventures, enabling rivals to collaborate on research while competing on production. Over 300 R&D joint ventures have been registered under the Act, with concentration in information technology, biotechnology and new materials.
source_quote: These are purely social risks, as the private risks of triple damages were eliminated by the 1984 National Co-operative Research Act. After a slow start, the latest count shows that over 300 R&D joint ventures have been registered under the Act, with concentration in information technology, biotechnology and new materials.

growth_orientation_rationale: Public-private R&D consortium in semiconductors addresses coordination failures between chip makers and equipment producers, improving industry-wide technological capability and competitiveness.
status_evidence: Sematech was launched in 1987 and funded jointly by the industry and the Department of Defence. Its major success has been to improve communications between its chip-making members and equipment producers.
importance_rationale: Significant sectoral R&D initiative combining public and private funding in a strategically important industry (semiconductors). Demonstrates a model for addressing coordination failures in pre-competitive research, though narrower in scope than system-wide reforms.
description: Sematech, a $200 million semiconductor R&D joint venture launched in 1987, was funded jointly by the semiconductor industry and the Department of Defence. Its major success has been to improve communications between its chip-making members and equipment producers.
source_quote: The most publicised case is that of the $200 million Semiconductor Manufacturing Technology (Sematech), launched in 1987 and funded jointly by the industry and the Department of Defence. Its major success has been to improve communications between its chip-making members and equipment producers.

growth_orientation_rationale: R&D tax credits reduce the effective cost of private R&D investment, incentivizing firms to increase innovation spending and productivity-enhancing research.
status_evidence: Text states 'proposed to extend', indicating announcement but not yet legislated or implemented.
importance_rationale: Significant extension of an existing major tax instrument with substantial fiscal cost ($17 billion over five years), but not a structural system-wide change.
description: The Administration proposed to extend the Research and Experimentation tax credit, which was scheduled to expire at the end of fiscal 1995, at a cost of $17 billion over five years and subject to pay-as-you-go budget rules.
source_quote: First, a number of tax provisions are scheduled to expire before the end of the budget planning horizon in 1999 (most prominently the Research and Experimentation tax credit at the end of fiscal 1995)... The total cost involved would be $17 billion over the next five years.

growth_orientation_rationale: Combines venture capital support for joint ventures and sectoral technology development, both of which enhance innovation capacity, firm formation, and productivity growth.
component_name: Venture capital and flat-panel display technology support
status_evidence: Text indicates the Act 'provides' funding, but no explicit evidence of legislative passage or implementation.
importance_rationale: Comprehensive legislative package with $1.9 billion in funding across multiple innovation support mechanisms (venture capital, government-industry collaboration, sectoral R&D), representing a significant structural initiative.
description: The National Competitiveness Act provides $1.9 billion for closer government-industry ties, including a $100 million venture capital provision for joint ventures and nearly $600 million for flat-panel display technology development.
source_quote: A so-called National Competitiveness Act is also being debated in the Congress. Its latest version provides $1.9 billion for forging closer ties between the government and industry. A venture capital provision provides $100 million for government participation of up to five years duration in joint ventures where the grant recipients pay at least half of all costs. Nearly $600 million of the total would go to flat-panel displays, a test case for the new, more activist technology policy.

growth_orientation_rationale: Extended patent terms strengthen intellectual property protection, incentivizing private R&D investment and commercialization; streamlined procedures reduce transaction costs for innovators.
status_evidence: Text states 'agreed to', indicating announcement of policy agreement but no explicit evidence of legislative passage or implementation.
importance_rationale: Significant reform of the patent system affecting the incentive structure for innovation and commercialization, but not a structural overhaul of the innovation system.
description: The United States agreed to extend patent terms to 20 years from the date of application (compared with 17 years from the date of grant), ease patent protest procedures, and make patent applications open for public inspection 18 months after submission.
source_quote: Over the summer an agreement was reached in the area of patents: for its part the United States agreed to extend patent terms to 20 years from the date of application as compared with 17 years from the date of grant; to ease the process of protesting the granting of a patent; and to make patent applications open for public inspection 18 months after submission.

growth_orientation_rationale: Reduces information asymmetries and regulatory barriers in angel capital markets, improving capital allocation to innovative startups and supporting entrepreneurial growth.
status_evidence: Text states 'the SBA has taken the initiative to create the Angel Capital Electronic Network (ACE-Net)' and describes it as operational with State Securities Administrators having agreed to remove restrictions.
importance_rationale: A significant initiative addressing a structural gap in startup financing by creating a nation-wide platform and removing inter-state regulatory barriers, with meaningful implications for angel capital market development.
description: The SBA created the Angel Capital Electronic Network (ACE-Net), a nation-wide Internet listing of small innovative companies with restricted access to angels, and coordinated with State Securities Administrators to remove inter-state trading restrictions on unregistered stocks of ACE-Net companies.
source_quote: In these circumstances, the SBA has taken the initiative to create the Angel Capital Electronic Network (ACE-Net). This is a nation-wide Internet listing of small innovative companies with the access restricted to angels.

growth_orientation_rationale: Supports commercialisation of scientific discoveries and increases high-risk research, bridging the gap between research and enterprise to accelerate innovation-driven growth.
status_evidence: Text describes ATP as an existing programme that has been evaluated, indicating it is operational.
importance_rationale: A significant direct support instrument for private-sector innovation and commercialisation, though evaluation results were disputed and impact remains uncertain.
description: The Advanced Technology Program (ATP) provides funding to assist US businesses to apply or commercialise new scientific discoveries, with the goal of increasing high-risk research and forging stronger links between the research community and enterprise.
source_quote: ATP provides funding to assist US businesses to apply or commercialise new scientific discoveries. A Department of Commerce evaluation found that the ATP increased high-risk research, implying that stronger links were being forged between the research community and enterprise.

growth_orientation_rationale: Facilitates technology transfer and adoption of modern technologies among small manufacturers, improving productivity and competitiveness, though awareness and uptake barriers limit impact.
status_evidence: Text describes MEP as an established nation-wide network with operational centres and survey data on user satisfaction, indicating it is in operation.
importance_rationale: A significant nation-wide technology transfer and diffusion programme with demonstrated positive effects on user firms, though limited awareness constrains overall impact.
description: The Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MEP) is a nation-wide network of locally managed manufacturing extension centres dedicated to helping smaller manufacturers improve competitiveness by adopting modern technologies, initially designed to transfer advanced technologies from government research institutes.
source_quote: MEP is a nation-wide network of locally managed manufacturing extension centres dedicated to helping smaller manufacturers improve their competitiveness by adopting modern technologies.

growth_orientation_rationale: Science parks can generate economic development and high job creation when successful, but high failure rates (approximately 50% of parks closed) and reliance on attracting external firms rather than generating spinoffs create significant inefficiencies and uncertain returns on public investment.
status_evidence: During the 1980s, many sub-national governments looked to technological development to revive their local economies and create jobs through the creation of science parks.
importance_rationale: Science parks represent a significant sub-national innovation policy initiative spanning multiple states, with substantial public investment in infrastructure and fiscal incentives. However, the assessment notes high failure rates and limited evidence of effectiveness, suggesting mixed systemic impact despite broad geographic reach.
description: Science parks were promoted by sub-national US governments during the 1980s as a strategy to support technological development and create high-tech jobs. These parks feature industry-driven R&D activities, links with research facilities (universities or institutes), and are supported through infrastructure provision, tax breaks, and fiscal incentives.
source_quote: Science parks are a type of business park where the primary activity of the majority of the establishments is industry-driven R&D. State and local authorities support science parks through the provision of infrastructure and land, tax breaks and tax holidays, promotion – primarily through marketing campaigns and lobbying – and other fiscal and physical incentives.
